references.text: Aaron goes out to meet Moses in the wilderness, as the Lord said in verse 14
The Lord's anger burns against Moses, just as his anger had burned against Miriam and Aaron
Aaron's genealogy as a Levite, son of Amram and Jochebed from the tribe of Levi
Aaron is appointed as Moses' spokesman to Pharaoh, fulfilling the promise in 4:14
Moses' objection regarding his lack of eloquence, which leads to the Lord's anger
Another instance where the Lord's anger burns against the people
Aaron is referred to as Miriam's brother, confirming the family relationship
Stephen's speech refers to Moses being sent as leader and deliverer
Aaron is mentioned as an example of how God calls people to priestly service
Aaron is appointed as priest, a role built upon his function as Moses' spokesman
7:1 shows the fulfillment of 4:14 by confirming Aaron's status as prophet for Moses.
Creates a clear contrast between God's appointment of the pair (4:14) and the people's later jealousy toward them.
10:3 demonstrates the practical execution of the roles established in 4:14.
Highlights the recurring dynamic in leadership where Aaron serves as Moses' spokesman to the people.
Creates a theological contrast between Aaron's role as a faithful 'brother' and the people's betrayal of their own brothers.
